decision: Round 2 of r15: Savar liked A (struck price on the card) most, but nothing stood out. Which price-led treatment of '30% off your first month' should ship?
primary_axis: how the first-month price is framed on the card (and once in the hero)
invariants: math plan only, CAD 99 a month
hero fact line: 'First month CAD 69.30, then CAD 99/month' (except J)
visual only: checkout and Stripe still charge CAD 99
run: npm run dev, then open /?variant=A|F|G|H|I|J (floating bar or left/right arrow keys)

options.name: Struck price (round 1 reference)
options.cost: Big number is not the monthly price
options.risk: Jump to 99 can feel like a trick

options.name: Two prices side by side
options.bet: First month CAD 69.30 -> every month after CAD 99, both prices on one line
options.benefit: Both numbers up front; no surprise later

options.name: Receipt
options.bet: A paper receipt: workbooks 99, delivery 0, 30% off -29.70, you pay 69.30
options.benefit: Shows the saving as a line item; paper fits the brand; delivery CAD 0 is visible
options.risk: Reads as checkout detail, not a headline

options.name: Red pen correction
options.bet: CAD 99 crossed out in red pen with 69.30 handwritten, like a teacher marking a page
options.benefit: Most memorable; ties the offer to marking work on paper
options.cost: Handwriting is harder to scan than type
options.risk: Can look informal or like a sale tag

options.name: Offer band on the card
options.bet: A colour band on top of the card carries the offer; the card stays CAD 99; button says 'Claim 30% off'
options.benefit: Loud but separate from the real price

options.name: Offer beside the hero button
options.bet: A price block under the hero buttons (CAD 69.30, CAD 99 struck); pricing card is A
options.benefit: The offer is above the fold, next to the action
options.risk: Hero starts to feel like a sales page
